problem_statement: Implement `fmt_time_tm_iso8601(char out[20], const struct tm *tm, char separator)` and `scn_time_tm_iso8601(struct tm *tm, const char *str, char separator)`. The first writes an ISO 8601 string into @p out as zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD<separator>HH:MM:SS, using the supplied separator between the date and time, and returns the number of characters written; the full length is 19. It should return -EINVAL for year values that cannot be represented in the four-digit year field. The second parses a string of the same form into @p tm, storing the calendar year in tm_year as year - 1900 and the month in tm_mon as month - 1. It returns 19 when a time part is present and 10 when only a date is present, returns -EBADF if a separator is present but is not the supplied one, and returns -EINVAL for malformed digit or separator patterns. It is not required to reject semantically invalid dates such as month 13 or minute 60 when the textual format is valid.

verification.reason: The original statement is mostly complete, but it omits the header where the API must be visible, NUL termination, and the fact that the formatter also must not reject semantically invalid date/time fields. These can be repaired by specifying the public interface and observable behaviour.

problems.detail: The hidden test includes fmt.h and calls the new functions, but the statement does not say they must be declared in sys/include/fmt.h.
The hidden unit test compares the formatted output as a C string, which requires a terminating NUL in the 20-byte buffer, but the statement only says the length is 19.

The statement does not make clear that fmt_time_tm_iso8601 must accept semantically invalid values such as minute or second 60; only the parsing function is described as not requiring semantic validation.
The statement says semantic invalid dates are not required to be rejected, but the hidden tests require them to be accepted; this needs to be expressed as observable behaviour.

problem_statement_fixed: Implement `fmt_time_tm_iso8601(char out[20], const struct tm *tm, char separator)` and `scn_time_tm_iso8601(struct tm *tm, const char *str, char separator)`, declared in `sys/include/fmt.h`. The first writes an ISO 8601 string into @p out as zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD<separator>HH:MM:SS, using the supplied separator between the date and time, and returns the number of characters written; the full length is 19. The 19 characters must be followed by a terminating '\0' in the 20-byte buffer. It should return -EINVAL for year values that cannot be represented in the four-digit year field (the calendar year `tm_year + 1900` must be 0000 to 9999). It should not reject semantically invalid values such as month 13 or minute/second 60 when those values are representable as two digits. The second parses a string of the same form into @p tm, storing the calendar year in tm_year as year - 1900 and the month in tm_mon as month - 1. It returns 19 when a time part is present and 10 when only a date is present, returns -EBADF if a separator is present but is not the supplied one, and returns -EINVAL for malformed digit or separator patterns. It should not reject semantically invalid dates such as month 13 or minute 60 when the textual format is valid.
